newsitem.title: USA: ConAgra first quarter earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: ConAgra first quarter earnings rise.

text.p: ConAgra Inc. said earnings for its first quarter rose, despite slightly lower sales and lower beef selling prices.

The Omaha, Neb.-based manufacturer of processed foods, meat, poultry and agriculture-related products said it earned $96.1 million, or 42 cents a share in the first quarter ended August 25, compared to $87.1 million, or 36 cents a share.
Sales were $6.40 billion for the quarter, compared to $6.44 billion the year before.
"Our people achieved record earnings despite exceptionally high and volatile grain prices," said Philip Fletcher, ConAgra's chief executive officer.
"For the full year, we continue to expect double-digit earnings per share growth and ConAgra's 17th consecutive year of record earnings," he said.
Profits rose in ConAgra's grocery and diversified products segments and food inputs and ingredients unit. Profits fell in the company's beef and refrigerated foods segments.
The company said it expects significant profit growth in its refrigerated foods in the second half of the year, as well as for the full year.
Sales in the refrigerated foods segment fell in the first quarter, due to lower selling prices for beef and the sale or closing of beef and poultry businesses.
The company said grain merchandising was the largest source of profit growth at its food input and ingredients segment.
Earnings from crop inputs such as fertiliser and chemicals used for pest control declined as a result of weather related planting delays that put off farmers' need for such items.
